selected_source_bindings.selected_text: The Typed Connection Extension Rule requires every global Relation Kind to expose a finite closed set of exact ordered source-kind to target-kind connections. A proposed extension must bind one effective predecessor Relation Kind version, one source endpoint contract, one target endpoint contract, direction, global scope, an exact qualifier schema with pair-specific values and constraints, canonical relation authority, contestability, owner, evidence, lifecycle effect, validation effect, and the exact successor contract version. Ontology-local connections must remain scoped to their exact Ontology contract. No global connection is created by endpoint registration, separate source and target lists, wildcard matching, historical observation, local graph use, shared naming, candidate validation, endpoint admission, or a second writable projection.

selected_source_bindings.subject: cal.definition.cyberalchemy-define@1.0.0-candidate.4
selected_source_bindings.selected_text:
Product Capability is the normalized definition identified by semantic.product-capability, owned within scope.product, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D67 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Product Capability is a stable, owner-qualified statement of an outcome that
one Product must enable for named participants or consumers while preserving
explicit scope, contracts, context policies, evidence routes, and authority
limits. It states what the Product must make possible and why that behavior
belongs to the Product. It does not select the agent, component, command,
interface, workflow, or implementation that realizes the outcome.

Every Product Capability belongs to exactly one Product. Its identity remains
stable while realizations, interfaces, evidence, and implementation technology
change, provided the outcome, Product anchor, scope, and owner boundary remain
the same. A material change to any of those anchors requires a successor
Product Capability rather than a silent rewrite.
selected_source_bindings.target_use: selected source clause/meaning boundaries; no source truth or new effect authority

selected_source_bindings.subject: cal.definition.cyberalchemy-define@1.0.0-candidate.4
selected_source_bindings.selected_text: A Method is a governed repeatable transformation whose scope, inputs, actions, roles, gates, outputs, evidence, residue rule, validation rule, recomposition rule, and boundary are explicit. A named Method specializes this form without inheriting authority to execute.

selected_source_bindings.subject: cal.definition.cyberalchemy-define@1.0.0-candidate.4
selected_source_bindings.selected_text:
Intent is the normalized definition identified by semantic.intent, owned within scope.coordination, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D39 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Intent is the declared purpose, desired capability, problem pressure, or change
direction that orients a CyberAlchemy v2 method before the exact output shape,
artifact, gate, or implementation path is fully settled.

Intent must be attributable, bounded enough to route, revisable under discovery,
and traceable to the artifacts, decisions, residue, or next routes that claim to
satisfy it. An intent may be refined, split, renamed, or rejected, but it must
not be silently replaced by an artifact or implementation convenience.

selected_source_bindings.subject: cal.definition.cyberalchemy-define@1.0.0-candidate.4
selected_source_bindings.selected_text:
Context View is the normalized definition identified by semantic.context-view, owned within scope.context-resolution, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D66 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Context View is an immutable, digest-bound projection produced by resolving one Context Request against one exact Context identity and source epoch; it records included and excluded material, lineage, limitations, and expiry or refresh conditions without becoming the Context itself.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified boundary of relevance
and interpretation for one declared purpose. It names the Product, optional
Project, optional Goal, intended consumers and uses, subject scope, and source
policies that frame what information and meaning may be assembled for the work.

Every CyberAlchemy Context belongs to exactly one Product. A project Context
belongs to exactly one Project. A goal Context belongs to exactly one Project
and focuses on exactly one Goal that already belongs to that Project. The first
contract intentionally allows only one primary Goal per Context; cross-goal
work requires separate Contexts or a later explicitly defined composite model.

A Context identity remains stable across new source epochs, resolution
requests, immutable views, interface presentations, session pauses, and
refreshes that preserve its Product, Project, Goal, and purpose. A material
change to any of those anchors creates a successor Context and supersedes the
earlier one instead of silently changing what the earlier identity meant.
